headline: Majors in overbought momentum above the 200-day line, but whale flows and positioning reveal persistent supply onto exchanges over four straight weeks.
paragraphs: Seven of seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving average, and all seven show MACD above signal line, marking a uniformly bullish regime by trend. However, the momentum meter is screaming overbought: Bitcoin's RSI is 82.5, Ethereum's is 79.5, and Solana's is 86.7, among the most extreme readings a technician can see. This is not a sign of weakness by itself, but it is a condition worth naming. The absence of a golden cross in any major (price above 50-day, 50-day above 200-day) tells you the uptrend is steep and recent rather than slowly building. Bitcoin has moved 25.85 percent over the last seven days and 27.35 percent over the last thirty, which explains both the RSI and the heavy distance from the 12-month high: at 36.4 percent below the peak of 124,739, the asset has room, but it is not starting from capitulation lows. Ethereum, Solana, and Cardano are each 47 to 76 percent below their 12-month peaks, leaving more absolute room, yet their 30-day moves are equally aggressive (31 to 39 percent).

Funding on the perp side is uniform and cheap: every major (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Doge) is paying exactly 0.01 percent every eight hours, annualizing to 11 percent. That is historically mild, not the sign of a crowded leveraged rally. Open interest is substantial, Bitcoin at 2.29 billion and Ethereum at 1.54 billion on OKX alone, but the positioning is not extreme: Bitcoin's long-to-short ratio is 1.02 (roughly balanced), while Solana is 1.54 and XRP is 1.71 (more longs, but not dislocated). The outlier is Doge at 3.31-to-1 longs, where short covers would matter, yet Doge's open interest is only 97.6 million, the smallest of the cohort. Liquidations over the last 18 to 24 hours total roughly 1,600 to 1,300 events per asset, with shorts taking the heavier blows in Bitcoin (9.1 million to 6.7 million long), confirming the directional bias of recent moves but not warning of a blow-off cascade.

The tension sits in whale flows and the stablecoin float. Over the last 24 hours, 56.9 million dollars in Bitcoin moved onto Coinbase, the biggest single transfer in the data window. More important, the pattern persists: the week ending August 25 saw 742 million dollars net onto exchanges, the third straight week of inflows after a brief outflow in the week of August 4 (1.017 billion off exchanges). Over a month, therefore, whales have moved more than 480 million dollars net onto venues, against a background of spot ETF inflows that continue: Bitcoin saw 337.6 million dollars on August 24 (six straight positive days, 1.958 billion over the last five sessions) and Ethereum saw 115.6 million (also six straight positive days, 777.3 million over five sessions). The stablecoin float is nearly flat at 308.7 billion, with a 30-day change of just 0.11 percent, meaning dry powder is neither accumulating nor fleeing.

Sentiment has rotated sharply into greed: the Fear and Greed index stands at 74, the high of its 30-day range. Against this, the tape shows supply being staged at exchange doorways (the four-week whale inflow chain and the daily Coinbase move) even as traditional finance continues to bid spot ETFs. This is a textbook disagreement: the crowd is in euphoria and buying spot, while whales are liquidating into the bid and moving the proceeds to trade venues. The daily close of Ethereum at exactly its 50-day high price is worth noting (2,481.51), and Bitcoin's failure to golden-cross despite its strength suggests the trend, while steep, may be running into its own momentum.

Watch for the reversal of the whale flow pattern: if the next weekly report shows net outflows from exchanges instead of inflows, the supply stage will have been exhausted and the picture will have changed. Monitor funding for any rise above the current 11 percent annual rate, which would signal longs paying to hold; any material flush of shorts in liquidations would confirm the trend's persistence. Bitcoin's reclaim of the 12-month high (124,739) would erase the 36.4 percent buffer and stamp this move as historic; any close below recent support would be the first real test of the three-week rally.
